title: Synthetic load surge triggered quota-plane threshold amplification and client backoff guidelines
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: During a routine chaos test in a partner region we observed a synthetic traffic spike that interacted with the quota-plane threshold smoothing algorithm and client-side retry heuristics to amplify ingress bursts. The result was a sustained 429 surge for ~27 minutes affecting a cohort of production tokens and several high-traffic customers. This ticket coordinates investigation findings, immediate mitigations implemented, and follow-up engineering and developer guidance work to prevent recurrence and reduce customer impact
timeline: 2025-11-03T09:12Z - Synthetic load generator in us-west-2 increased ramp from 200rps to 8k rps over 90s as part of a pressure test
2025-11-03T09:14Z - Gateway quota-plane observed threshold crossings and started aggressive clamp decisions (quota smoothing disabled in edge config due to recent rollout)
2025-11-03T09:16Z - Clients saw early 429s and many SDKs began immediate aggressive retries (default exponential backoff misconfigured for SDK v1.3 => 0 retry jitter)
2025-11-03T09:20Z - Spike amplified due to retry storms; control plane counters reported token-level overcounting and leader heartbeat jitter
2025-11-03T09:39Z - SRE runbook executed: throttles relaxed, synthetic generator paused, and temporary rate-limiter safety leash applied cluster-wide
2025-11-03T09:40Z - Error rates declined; partial recovery by 09:47Z after safety leash fully rolled out
impact: Affected customers: 14 tenants with heavy bursty traffic patterns; 6 enterprise tenants experienced notable tail latencies and elevated error budgets
Symptoms: widespread 429s, increased p99 latency for gateway, dashboards showing token count oscillations and retry amplification
root_cause: A confluence of three factors produced the amplification: (1) a synthetic ramp test introduced a rapid ingress burst; (2) a recent config change disabled quota smoothing on the quota-plane in several regions (intended to reduce steady-state latency) which removed the system's damping; (3) an SDK regression in v1.3 removed jitter from exponential backoff, causing synchronized client retries. Individually these were non-critical; combined they created a feedback loop that amplified the burst and made quota clamps act aggressively, misattributing retries as new inbound work and prolonging the event.
immediate_remediation: Rolled back quota smoothing config to previous stable profile in affected regions (09:22Z)
Engaged emergency safety leash on quota-plane to cap per-token clamp rate (09:25Z)
Paused synthetic load generator and coordinated with partner test owners (09:28Z)
Released hotfix #PR-1220 to restore client-side jitter recommendation in SDK v1.3.x (09:50Z)
long_term_actions: Restore quota smoothing but add a canary flag and automated rollback when oscillation metrics exceed threshold (owner: A. Kapoor, estimate: 5)
Introduce a throttle-propagation limiter to avoid counting retry-attempts as new work until a short deduplication window expires (owner: S. Martinez, estimate: 8)
Add SDK release gating tests that simulate quota-plane clamps and assert presence of randomized backoff+jitter (owner: Developer Experience, estimate: 3)
Create public customer guidance and update SDK migration notes describing safe retry defaults and how to opt into conservative retry logic (owner: PM - Noah Patel, estimate: 2)
Build an observability alert that flags retry amplification patterns (ratio of retries->new tokens over 90s) and triggers automated safety leash (owner: SRE, estimate: 5)
Schedule a runbook walkthrough with on-call teams to rehearse synthetic burst scenarios and coordination with partners (owner: SRE Lead, estimate: 2)
Audit recent region config rollouts for changes that touch smoothing/threshold logic and add preflight checks (owner: Config Safety, estimate: 4)
